locate.rankedHypotheses:
H1 (PRIME, ★★★★★): the bf16 `in_proj_ba` GEMM is M-keyed -> a/b (= scan raw_a/raw_b -> gate b_g/b_beta) shift on the spine row. Evidence: (a) it is the ONLY GDN GEMM not proven M-invariant; (b) checkpoint /models/qwen3.6-27b-fp8 config.json puts `linear_attn.in_proj_a`+`in_proj_b` in `modules_to_not_convert` (371 entries) => bf16 cuBLAS, not fp8; (c) `LUMO_FB_BATCH_INVARIANT_BA_PROJ` (gdn_linear_attn.py:553-601) was purpose-built to pad the ba projection to a fixed row group "so the BA projection shape is independent across active K" = existence proof it is M-variant (and it is OFF in the locked launcher); (d) Thinking Machines #42960: at small M/N libraries switch to Split-K, altering reduction order AND tensor-core tile selection -> exactly M=10 vs M=5; (e) the current SUBOP_MAB harness is BLIND to it (slices the M=10 ba output), so the prior "in_proj bit-exact" ruling (FR13_BRANCH_FLIP_LOCALIZED:21) is vacuous for this GEMM. Only candidate that is M-dependent AND upstream of the proven-M-invariant scan AND on the spine data path AND covered by vLLM BI's mm/linear override.
H2 (★★☆☆☆, dependent): conv bf16-tap/fused MAC carrying an M-keyed input. Refuted as INDEPENDENT carrier: conv is row-occupancy M-invariant (FR13_CONV_NOT_CARRIER) and consumes the fp8 q/k/v (M-invariant), NOT a/b -> cannot carry H1's perturbation. Clean control (predict ~0).
H3 (★☆☆☆☆, refuted-on-GB10): fp8 in_proj_qkvz M-dependence. fp8 block GEMM single-M-tile (M<=64 BLOCK_SIZE_M, K=128 pinned, no Spark cfg => get_w8a8_block_fp8_configs=None) = M-invariant (commit 2fe2c567). Keep as explicit fp8-control arm (predict ~0; nonzero = surprise that re-opens fp8).
H4 (★☆☆☆☆, refuted): cross-branch mask bleed in our tree-scan ancestry accumulator. Code shows select-by-where folds no leaf into spine; FR13_BV_GEOMETRY measured scan 0.0 vs native at N_PAD=1 AND 16. Kept only as the textbook STree failure mode; closed here.
H5 (★☆☆☆☆, n/a): chunk-boundary M-shift. Neither path chunks by tree_n (our scan = static_range(N_PAD); native = sequential for-loop; fp8 chunks K not M). No M-dependent row chunking.
H6 (★☆☆☆☆, refuted): state-feed/bank layout. Spine reads its own committed-path bank (spec_state_indices[:,0]/accepted_len-1 column), independent of leaf bank ids; bank geom-fix 8cdda4c4 confirmed h0_state_in BYTE-EXACT. Leaf banks occupy other columns the spine never reads.
locate.crossBranchBleed: The GDN tree-scan ancestry mask PERFECTLY isolates spine from leaves in our kernel src/lumo_flywheel_serving/fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py. Parent-state read at :459-467: `for j in static_range(0,i): ancestor=(strict_mask[i*N_PAD+j]!=0)&(j<N_ACTUAL); h_j=tl.sum(tl.where((offs_n==j),h_cache,0.0),axis=0); state_i=tl.where(ancestor,h_j,state_i)`. A spine node i adopts node j's checkpoint ONLY when strict_mask[i,j]==1 (j a true ancestor); off-spine leaf slots have strict_mask[spine,leaf]==0 -> never selected, so NO leaf state folds into a spine node's state. Mask built from Tree.ancestors (:43-51), correct by construction. The one co-mingling point is the gather reduction `tl.sum(tl.where(offs_n==j, h_cache, 0.0), axis=0)` (:463-466) over the FULL N_PAD slot axis, but non-j slots (incl leaves) are masked to exact 0.0 and the add tree is over a STATIC N_PAD extent (static_range), so populating leaf slots does NOT change the reduction tree or h_j bits. DECISIVE empirical: FR13_BV_GEOMETRY_NOT_THE_SEAM_BIND shows our _tree_gdn_kernel = 0.0 vs native at N_PAD=1 AND N_PAD=16 (cat9 size) on captured spine inputs. A leaf CANNOT bleed into a spine node state. So the +17 is NOT a mask bug; it is an upstream input-projection M-dependence (H1) that makes the spine's q/k/v/a/b themselves M-variant BEFORE the bit-exact scan consumes them.
locate.gemmMDependence:
in_proj_qkvz (q,k,v,z): fp8 w8a8 block-scaled (w8a8_triton_block_scaled_mm custom op), spine row M-INVARIANT — default cfg BLOCK_SIZE_M=64/GROUP_SIZE_M=32/BLOCK_SIZE_K=128-pinned; M=10 and M=5 both fit one M-tile (M<=64) so the fp32 K-accum `accumulator += tl.dot*a_s*b_s` over range(cdiv(K,128)) runs identical tile-count/order; no split-K at tiny M; fp8 M-keyed cfg lookup dead on GB10 (no Spark JSON). 
in_proj_ba (-> a,b = scan raw_a/raw_b): bf16 UnquantizedLinearMethod -> cuBLAS/cuBLASLt mm/linear (in_proj_a/_b in fp8 checkpoint modules_to_not_convert). SPINE ROW M-VARIANT (suspected carrier) — cuBLASLt heuristic kernel + split-K selection differs M=10 vs M=5 -> different fp32 reduction order -> ~1 bf16-ULP shift in a/b. THIS IS THE bf16-batch-variant GEMM. Existence proof: LUMO_FB_BATCH_INVARIANT_BA_PROJ scaffolding built for it. 
o_proj (out_proj): fp8 block-scaled, M-INVARIANT (same single-M-tile argument) AND post-scan (cannot feed recurrent state) -> cannot be carrier. 
gate (RMSNormGated norm(core_attn_out,z)): bf16 elementwise, row-local -> M-invariant per row, not a GEMM. 
Locked launcher fr13_launch_locked.sh: BATCH_INVARIANT=0, LUMO_FB_KERNEL_ROWS unset -> bf16 in_proj_ba runs in default M-keyed cuBLAS in the deployed path.
locate.chunkBoundary: No. Neither the tree forward nor native verify forwards rows in an M-dependent chunking that shifts the spine row. Our tree-scan = per-node static_range(N_PAD) where N_PAD is fixed per family by padded_nodes() (pow2 ceil, NOT data chunking). Native verify (fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update_kernel) = sequential `for i_t in range(0,T)` over flat rows (no chunk). The fp8 GEMM chunks only K (=128, fixed), not M. So the spine row's chunk membership / reduction order does not move when leaves are added. The only M-keyed reduction-order change is the bf16 in_proj_ba GEMM's INTERNAL split-K (that is H1, not a row-chunk-boundary effect).
locate.stateFeedGeom: No. Leaf rows do NOT change the spine row's cache bank/column reads. The spine reads its prior recurrent/conv state from the committed-path bank (spec_state_indices[b,0], or column accepted_len-1), which is node-indexed and independent of leaf bank ids. The bank geom-fix (8cdda4c4/d30755c8) confirmed the deep-row prior read is in-range and h0_state_in is BYTE-EXACT across the carrier event. Leaf bank ids occupy OTHER columns of spec_state_indices that the spine never dereferences. Adding leaves changes which banks exist in non-spine columns but not the spine's own bank/column reads.

locate.isolateFixDirection:
Goal: make the input-projection M-invariant so the spine row's a/b (and q/k/v) are bit-identical regardless of leaf count -> the proven-bit-exact scan then yields a bit-exact spine output (leaves accept WITHOUT perturbing the spine). If A/B confirms H1 (bf16 in_proj_ba):
(1) PREFERRED, scaffolding exists: enable LUMO_FB_BATCH_INVARIANT_BA_PROJ (LUMO_FB_KERNEL_ROWS=1 + a fixed LUMO_FB_PROJ_PAD_ROWS) so the ba GEMM always runs at a FIXED M (pad spine+leaves to a constant tree_n-independent row group, scatter real rows back) -> pins cuBLASLt kernel/split-K to one shape -> M-invariant a/b. NOTE: the existing impl pads across the spec-decode batch (nspec) dim; for the B=1 width problem it must be RE-SCOPED to pin the within-spec tree_n row dim to a constant (e.g. always pad to N_PAD=16 rows). Lossless by construction (padded rows discarded; real rows' math unchanged-shape), NOT a reroute.
(2) Narrower: wrap only in_proj_ba.forward under enable_batch_invariant_mode (or a fixed-config cuBLASLt heuristic) so its bf16 GEMM uses a batch-invariant kernel; fp8 GEMMs untouched. The C1 fix made surgical.
(3) Most code: compute a/b for the committed spine at a fixed M (spine rows padded to constant N_PAD), leaves projected separately — genuinely-isolated spine compute (the leaves still get their own M-invariant-padded projection + still verify; only the GEMM SHAPE the spine sees is frozen), NOT a copy/route-around.
If H3 (only on a measured surprise): fp8 custom-op BI override (fixed BLOCK_SIZE_M/GROUP_SIZE_M/num_warps independent of M, K-loop already fixed), FR13_GB10_FP8_GEMV_CFG-class made M-pinned. BANNED (feedback_no_reroute_reward_hacking): routing spine through native non-tree GEMM, copying spine a/b from a separate clean run, dense recompute, splice. Fix must make OUR co-resident projection bit-invariant, not avoid co-residency.
locate.onlineFindings:
Thinking Machines "Defeating Nondeterminism in LLM Inference" (#42960 family): batch-invariance breaks in matmul because at small M/N libraries switch to Split-K (parallel reductions along K), altering reduction ORDER and even instruction selection (tensor-core TILE sizes) — EXACTLY our M=10-vs-M=5 bf16 in_proj_ba regime; fix = fix kernel config regardless of batch shape (= isolate-fix #1/#2). They ship batch-invariant-ops (drop-in mm/RMSNorm/softmax) integrated with vLLM deterministic mode -> 1000 runs bit-identical. vLLM enable_batch_invariant_mode overrides only ATEN ops (covers bf16 mm/linear=in_proj_ba; does NOT cover the fp8 custom op) — which is why C1's outcome cleanly distinguishes bf16-carrier from fp8-carrier. 
STree (arXiv 2505.14969, Speculative Tree Decoding for Hybrid SSMs): packs tree nodes into one sequence + attention mask; named risk = cross-branch contamination of a SHARED recurrent accumulator; they enforce PER-PATH state accumulation so leaves cannot retroactively alter spine state. Our kernel already enforces this via strict-mask select-by-where (H4 closed) — our +17 is NOT the STree shared-accumulator bug; it is a numeric (sub-ULP, M-keyed-GEMM) INPUT perturbation, a class STree's algebraic isolation does not address. 
Mamba Drafters (2506.01206)/SpecMamba (2509.19873): SSM decode compresses history into fixed-size state, impeding backtracking — reinforces that the recurrent state is the AMPLIFIER (tiny input perturbation -> state drift over depth/layers). 
Gated DeltaNet (ICLR 2025)/Yang 2406.06484: chunked vs recurrent are R-equal not bit-exact (fp non-assoc) = the SEPARATE +2 oracle-frame gap, kept distinct from the +17. 
GB10: 273 GB/s LPDDR5X unified mem, B=1 decode bandwidth-bound; the fixed-M ba-pad fix adds only a constant pad to a fixed-shape GEMM (no extra weight DMA) -> effectively free on the bandwidth budget vs decode weight streaming, so M-invariance does not cost the cat9>native E5 B=1 speed bar.

verify.topHypothesis: H1 — the bf16 `in_proj_ba` GEMM is M-keyed, perturbing the spine row's a/b (scan raw_a/raw_b → gate b_g/b_beta) when leaves co-reside. DECISIVE code evidence, all verified live: (a) checkpoint /models/qwen3.6-27b-fp8/config.json — I confirmed `in_proj_a`/`in_proj_b` ARE in `modules_to_not_convert` (371 entries, weight_block_size=[128,128]) while `in_proj_qkvz` is NOT → in_proj_ba is bf16 cuBLAS/cuBLASLt, in_proj_qkvz is fp8; reinforced by gdn_linear_attn.py:303 "ba_proj doesn't support blockwise fp8 quantization". (b) It is the ONLY GDN GEMM on the spine data path that is both M-dependent AND upstream of the proven-M-invariant scan: fp8 in_proj_qkvz/o_proj are single-M-tile M-invariant (get_w8a8_block_fp8_configs returns None on GB10 — no Spark JSON, line 1190; K-loop M-independent line 1127; M=10 and M=5 both ≤ BLOCK_SIZE_M=64), and o_proj is post-scan so it cannot feed recurrent state. (c) Existence proof of M-variance: the `LUMO_FB_BATCH_INVARIANT_BA_PROJ` scaffold (gdn_linear_attn.py:553-601) was purpose-built to pad the ba GEMM to a fixed row group "so the BA projection shape is independent across active K", and it is OFF in the locked launcher (scripts/fr13_launch_locked.sh:28 BATCH_INVARIANT=0, no LUMO_FB_KERNEL_ROWS). (d) The scan kernel is bit-exact to native on IDENTICAL captured inputs at N_PAD=1 AND N_PAD=16/cat9 (FR13_BV_GEOMETRY_NOT_THE_SEAM_BIND: D16=D32=0.0) — so the perturbation cannot be born in the scan; it must arrive in the inputs (a/b), which in_proj_ba produces. Mask-bleed (H4) is closed by code: fr10_gdn_tree_kernel.py:459-467 select-by-where with strict_mask folds no leaf state into a spine node (off-spine strict_mask[spine,leaf]=0, never selected; the tl.sum gather over static_range(N_PAD) masks non-j slots to exact 0.0 so leaf occupancy doesn't change the reduction tree). H2(conv)/H5(chunk)/H6(bank-geom) refuted by code as the doc states.
verify.rewardHackCheck: REAL FIX, not a route-around — passes the strict adversarial bar. The isolateFixDirection is M-invariance of the in_proj_ba GEMM: pad the projection to a FIXED, tree_n-independent M (constant row group), compute, scatter the real rows back, discard pads. This is mathematically the SAME per-row computation (a GEMM output row = W @ hidden_states[row], independent per row; zero pad-rows contribute nothing and are dropped) — it does NOT copy the spine's a/b from a separate clean run, does NOT densely recompute the spine in a non-tree forward, does NOT splice native non-tree output, does NOT reroute the spine through a different kernel. The leaves still get their own M-invariant-padded projection and still verify; only the GEMM SHAPE the spine sees is frozen. This is exactly the AUTHORIZED Thinking Machines #42960 prescription ("fix kernel config regardless of batch shape") and the same class as the banked batch-invariance work — distinct from the BANNED routes in feedback_no_reroute_reward_hacking. TWO caveats the GPU slot must honor: (1) the existing LUMO_FB scaffold pads across the spec-decode batch (nspec) dim and at B=1 nspec=1 so its `_lumo_fb_nspec > 1` guard FAILS and it is INERT — the doc correctly flags it must be RE-SCOPED to pin the within-spec tree_n row dim to a constant; do not assume the shipped scaffold solves the width problem. (2) bit-exactness of the padded real rows is an EMPIRICAL claim (playbook class 10: byte A/B, NEVER atol) — cuBLASLt could still pick a different kernel if the fixed pad M crosses a tile boundary differently; the fix's own A/B must verify byte-identical real-row output at the pinned M, not assume it.
verify.recommendation: EXTEND the harness before running the A/B — the present FR13_GDN_SUBOP_MAB will NOT discriminate H1 as-built. I verified scripts/fr10_phase4_patch_vllm_tree_gdn.py:3907 passes already-projected `a`,`b` (post-in_proj_ba at M=tree_n) into the harness, and every arm SLICES them (a0=a[start:end], b0=b[start:end] at :1423-1424; the conv arm index_selects pre_conv0 at :1487; the scan re-uses the sliced a/b). So pre_conv/conv1d_out/scan_out all consume the SAME M=10 in_proj_ba output and predict ~0.0 even if H1 is true — a class-12 vacuous-instrument trap. Add an in_proj_ba (and a control in_proj_qkvz) RE-RUN-at-reduced-M arm that re-invokes the projection from a captured PRE-projection hidden_states span (not a slice), with class-9 engagement asserts, then byte/int-view compare M10-vs-M5 on the deep-spine row (class 10, never atol). Predicted discriminating signature once extended: H1 → in_proj_ba re-run arm NONZERO (~1 bf16 ULP) while in_proj_qkvz re-run, conv1d_out, scan_out stay 0.0 (DECISIVE POSITIVE); H3 → in_proj_qkvz arm NONZERO (expect null); H4 → scan_out nonzero on identical inputs (expect 0.0, already competent); H2 → conv1d_out nonzero (expect 0.0). Cheap flag-only pre-screen C1 = cat9 + BATCH_INVARIANT=1 (pin BI on BOTH arms, class 11): 22→~5 ⇒ bf16 mm carrier = in_proj_ba; stays 22 ⇒ fp8 custom-op (re-opens H3) or diffuse → use the re-run arm. CAVEAT to flag for the slot: GB10 (sm_121/family-120) takes the REDUCED enable_batch_invariant_mode branch (FR13_BRANCH_FLIP_LOCALIZED:25-26), so C1 BI-on may not fully cover even the bf16 mm/linear if the reduced override set drops it — that is why the in_proj_ba re-run arm, not C1, is the mechanism-pinning instrument.
